newsitem.title: UK: IGC ups 1996 world coarse grains crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC ups 1996 world coarse grains crop estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday raised its estimate for 1996 world coarse grains production to 884 million tonnes from itse previous estimate of 881 million tonnes a month ago.

In its latest Grain Market Report, the IGC raised its estimate for Italian production by 800,000 tonnes to 11.6 million, added 500,000 tonnes to its estimate for Poland, bringing output to 16.5 million and raised its Mexican estimate to 24.9 million tonnes from 22.9 million.

Estimated production in former Yugoslavia was cut by 200,000 tonnes to 5.7 million while Argentina's output was cut by 100,000 tonnes to 17.5 million. Turkey's estimate was down 200,000 tonnes, to 9.8 million and South Africa's estimated production was cut by 300,000 tonnes to 8.7 million tonnes.

Almost all of the rise in estimated coarse grains production was accounted for by expanding ideas on maize. The IGC put world maize output in 1996 at 571.2 million tonnes (previous estimate 568.7 million). Its estimate for barley production was cut to 154.7 million tonnes (155.0 million).
Estimated sorghum production was raised to 64.2 million tonnes (63.9 million), while oats was up 200,000 tonnes at 31.3 million and rye up 100,000 tonnes at 24.2 million.
